synopsis: For brake-commanding earth-moving functions, the corpus identifies ISO 19014—not ISO 26262—as the functional-safety framework using MPLr; adding braking crosses the boundary from excluded awareness-only systems into motion-affecting safety control [f2071, f2075, f11993]. Validation therefore needs to address brake-command integrity, faults, degraded modes and unintended activation, with machine-control safety analysis determining required risk reduction and performance level; Part 5 supplies tabulated MPLr intended to avoid a full safety analysis for every new model [f5223, f10516, f2076]. The series covers hardware, software and environmental testing, including documented performance under expected environmental conditions, while ISO 19014-4 leaves cybersecurity to separate coverage [f322, f7735, f7488]. The review found no simulation-credibility acceptance criteria, statistical acceptance target or wording permitting virtual-only validation, but incomplete access to paid texts means these findings do not establish that replacing physical tests is prohibited [f5110, f324, f9459, f7544]. Parts 1–4 edition 2 and Part 5 edition 1 reached publication stage 60.00 in August 2026 with October publication scheduled, but a separate chapter lists 22 November 2026 for revised Part 1, so final status should be rechecked before design freeze and the plan should allow re-baselining [f2073, f7738, f6286, f10369]. For most markets, the internal safety board and customers accept validation evidence, but applicability to the particular machine, function and jurisdiction remains unresolved; an assessor-quality package should trace simulation claims to requirements or hazards and the final pass/fail argument [f1613, f10316, f8029].

Chapter 3 adds MPLr as the governing functional-safety measure.

Both require environmental qualification of safety-related electrical/electronic components under Part 3.
Both report Part 1 edition 2 under publication in October 2026.

Ongoing revisions motivate allowing a validation-plan re-baseline.
